title: The names crustacean shellfish hides behind
standfirst: Crustacean shellfish goes by many names on a label. Here is the list we read for you.

spans.text: The law makes a maker name crustacean shellfish when they put it in on purpose. It does not make them use the word you are looking for.

blocks.label: names we watch for on a label
blocks.caption: Counted only where the link to crustacean shellfish is settled. Names that depend on the product are listed further down, and are not in this count.

resolved.method: Names whose link to shellfish is settled, counted from our allergen registry.
resolved.excludedNote: 24 more depend on the product or are shared with something else, so they are listed separately rather than counted here.

sources.doc: Food Allergen Labeling and Consumer Protection Act of 2004 (FALCPA), Public Law 108-282, Title II — defines 'Crustacean shellfish' as a major food allergen; molluscan shellfish explicitly excluded from the major-allergen list
FASTER Act of 2021 (Public Law 117-11) — reaffirms the major allergen list, adds sesame as the 9th; crustacean shellfish remains a listed major allergen
Regulation (EU) No 1169/2011 on the provision of food information to consumers, Annex II — item 2 'Crustaceans and products thereof'; item 14 'Molluscs and products thereof' (separate allergen)
Scientific Opinion on the evaluation of allergenic foods and food ingredients for labelling purposes, EFSA Journal 12(11):3894 — crustacean allergens (tropomyosin) and derivation of hidden forms
Shellfish Allergy overview — crustacean species list and hidden sources (shrimp paste, seafood flavoring, glucosamine)
Villacis J. et al. and ACAAI guidance — glucosamine and chitosan are commonly manufactured from crustacean shells; shellfish-allergic consumers advised caution (origin not always declared)
Fish and Fishery Products Hazards and Controls Guidance — surimi/imitation crab may carry crab extract; crustacean must be declared when present

resolved.limit: We read what a label says. We cannot see what a maker left off it.

spans.text: These depend on the product. We treat them with care, and we say so on the label reading rather than guessing.
Names that look close but are not crustacean shellfish. These are the ones you can stop worrying about.
What we do when the label is unclear
If we cannot tell, we warn you. On this one thing we would rather be wrong in the direction of caution than quiet.
